details.title: Gulf Crown Hotels & Resorts Co. — Digital Transformation Programme
details.courts_or_seat: competent courts in the City of Riyadh, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

governing_law_source.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws and regulations in force in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

details.parties_quote:
1.1 Gulf Crown Hotels & Resorts Co., a closed joint stock company incorporated under the laws of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, holding Commercial Registration No. 1010584431, with its head office at King Fahd Road, Al Olaya District, P.O. Box 88214, Riyadh 11662, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (the "Company"); and

1.2 AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd, a private limited company incorporated under the laws of the Republic of India, bearing CIN U72900MH2019PTC321456, with its registered office at 4th Floor, Baner Business Bay, Pune 411045, Maharashtra, India (the "Service Provider").

payment_source.quote: The Company shall pay each undisputed invoice within sixty (60) days from the date of receipt of a valid invoice.

details.services_summary: Design, develop, test, deploy and support a revenue management and guest analytics platform for nine hotel properties in Saudi Arabia.

liability_cap.quote: Save in respect of liability arising from fraud, wilful misconduct, breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality) or Clause 13 (Data Protection), each Party's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the Contract Value.

delay_penalty.quote: Should the Service Provider fail to achieve any Milestone by its scheduled completion date, the Service Provider shall pay to the Company, by way of liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to one percent (1%) of the Contract Value for each week or part thereof of delay.

restrictive_covenants.summary: Deliverables specifically created for the Company become the property of the Company upon payment in full.
restrictive_covenants.restricted_activity: Assigning ownership of created deliverables prior to payment in full.
restrictive_covenants.quote: All Deliverables specifically created for the Company under this Agreement shall, upon payment in full, become the property of the Company.

findings.title: Al Noor Hospitality Group: Data analytics, AI or revenue-management services
findings.why: The new deal involves revenue-management services for a hospitality business in Saudi Arabia, which directly collides with the non-compete commitment for Al Noor covering hospitality businesses in Saudi Arabia.
findings.comparison: Do not take analytics, AI or revenue-management work for hotel groups in the GCC until about September 2029 without Al Noor's written consent.
findings.quote: the Supplier undertakes that neither it nor any of its Affiliates shall, during the Restricted Period, directly or indirectly, provide data analytics, artificial intelligence or revenue-management services to any Hospitality Business in the GCC.
findings.exception: Clause 12.4 lets Al Noor waive it per engagement by written consent. Waiver letter of 10 Feb 2026 allows only the Seaside Hotels (Muscat) demand-forecasting SOW; not follow-on SOWs, other hotels or Affiliates.

findings.title: Delay penalties calculated as percentage of total contract value
findings.why: Penalty is based on total contract value rather than milestone fees, risking disproportionate deductions.
findings.comparison: Past contracts like Acme and Northwind use milestone fees.
findings.quote: an amount equal to one percent (1%) of the Contract Value for each week or part thereof of delay.

findings.title: Indian entity under non-Indian law (Kingdom of Saudi Arabia)
findings.why: Disputes would be fought under foreign law and courts.
findings.comparison: Principle: India for AtliQ Pvt Ltd. Past exceptions (Al Noor DIFC, Northwind English law) were deliberate.
findings.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws and regulations in force in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

findings.title: Payment in 60 days
findings.why: Long payment terms hurt cash flow.
findings.quote: The Company shall pay each undisputed invoice within sixty (60) days from the date of receipt of a valid invoice.

findings.title: Termination for convenience limits payment
findings.why: Restricts payment only to 'accepted' services rather than all work done up to termination.
findings.comparison: AtliQ's principle requires payment for all work done, not just accepted deliverables.
findings.quote: The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' written notice, in which event the Company shall pay for all Services performed and accepted up to the date of termination.

findings.title: Liability cap excludes certain clauses from the aggregate limit
findings.why: Uncapped liability for confidentiality and data protection breaches creates high financial exposure for AtliQ.
findings.comparison: AtliQ principles prefer a standard 1x cap without carve-outs.
findings.quote: Save in respect of liability arising from fraud, wilful misconduct, breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality) or Clause 13 (Data Protection), each Party's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the Contract Value.

findings.title: One-sided IP indemnity provided by AtliQ
findings.why: AtliQ provides an unmutual IP indemnity protecting the client without a reciprocal indemnity for client-provided materials.
findings.comparison: Principles state indemnity should be mutual.
findings.quote: The Service Provider shall indemnify the Company against all losses, claims and expenses arising from any claim by a third party that the Deliverables infringe the intellectual property rights of such third party.

findings.title: Delay penalty exclusions only cover force majeure
findings.why: Fails to exclude client-caused delays or scope changes explicitly from delay penalties.
findings.comparison: Principles require excluding client-caused delays and scope changes.
findings.quote: The Service Provider shall not be liable for delay to the extent such delay is caused by a Force Majeure Event as defined in Clause 15.

findings.title: Strict data localization requirement in Saudi Arabia
findings.why: Restricts data hosting locations, which may conflict with AtliQ's standard cloud infrastructure and tools.
findings.comparison: Principles warn against data location limits.
findings.quote: Guest Data shall be hosted within the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia unless the Company provides prior written approval for any transfer outside the Kingdom.

findings.title: Arabic Text Prevails in Inconsistency
findings.why: AtliQ may not be able to easily review Arabic versions, creating hidden risks.
findings.comparison: Unusual compared to standard English-only governing language clauses.
findings.quote: In the event of any inconsistency, the Arabic text shall prevail.

findings.title: Transition assistance required on termination
findings.why: Imposes an obligation to provide up to 60 days of transition assistance without explicitly mentioning compensation.
findings.comparison: Past contracts usually compensate for ongoing transition work.
findings.quote: Upon termination, the Service Provider shall deliver to the Company all Deliverables and work in progress, and shall provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to sixty (60) days.

findings.title: Mandatory Cloud Hosting Within KSA Region
findings.why: Restricts hosting infrastructure choices to a specific geographical location.
findings.comparison: Data location limits must be checked against AtliQ hosting capabilities.
findings.quote: Cloud hosting within KSA region; availability target 99.5% monthly.
